worked_solution:
From the identity $1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =x-\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get 

$$
1-{sin}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})={cos}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}|\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})|\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{4})\,{|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
